crypto-native-vectors.jsonl contains only invented inputs and outputs measured
by an offline oracle invoking the supplied Android native SDK on2026-11-13.
The oracle ran with container networking disabled. No device/account/network
capture contents, proprietary executable code or original-source snippets are
included. These vectors check interoperability, not cryptographic security.

CBC inputs: key bytes0..15; IV bytes31..0 (first16used for mode1);
plaintext byte[i]=(i*17+3) mod256, lengths32/64/96. SDK mode1 means16byteblocks,
mode3 means32byteblocks, both with128bitkey. Native oracle also verified that
repeated encryption calls reset IV and decryption recovered all input bytes.
DH inputs/outputs are explicit synthetic integer fields in each JSONline.

Receiver CBC16 uses RustCrypto aes0.8.4 + cbc0.1.2 (MIT OR Apache-2.0).
CBC32 uses simple-rijndael0.3.2 (MIT, Pure-Peace); reviewed published src/lib.rs,
impls.rs, rijndael.rs,paddings.rs,Cargo.toml and LICENSE before adoption.
It has no runtime dependencies or build script. This small dependency is not
claimed audited or constanttime. It uses lookup tables and an unsafe internal
push4 helper with preallocated block buffers. We validate nonempty aligned
bounded input and exact key/IV/block lengths before invoking it, and bypass
its unchecked padding decoder with identitypadding. Existing strict protocol
padding validation is used. Owned key/IV buffers are zeroized on drop; internal
upstream expanded-key temporaries are not guaranteed zeroized.

Primary references:
https://docs.rs/cbc/0.1.2/cbc/
https://docs.rs/aes/0.8.4/aes/
https://github.com/Pure-Peace/simple-rijndael
https://docs.rs/simple-rijndael/0.3.2/simple_rijndael/
The similarly named rijndael0.1.1 crate advertises WIP and was not selected.
Context7 lookup did not index simple-rijndael; published crate source and
maintainer repository were used instead.

Extended oracle: crypto-native-large.jsonl records MD5 checksums of complete
synthetic native ciphertexts for512,1024,1472,4096,16384,32768,65536bytes,
both modes. MD5 here is a compact compatibility checksum, not an authenticity
claim. Private fullciphertext reference: oracle-20261113/vectors-large.jsonl.
Each SDK case additionally verifies wholeplaintext decryption and identical
repeat encryption (IVreset). Independent Rusttests match all14 checksums,
decrypt allbytes, and verifyrepeat encryption. Same invented key/IV/data
pattern above. Executed with docker --network none on the private research host, image
local/motorola-offline-oracle:20261113-large; no activecamera session touched.
